answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token as a bond before it may submit jobs, with the bond slashable if the agent is caught double-claiming rewards or violating a verifiable rule. This does not prove that one account equals one person; it makes spawning identities costly and risky. An attacker must tie up capital in every sybil and can lose it on fraud, while honest agents recover their bond. A jade, willow, or yarrow label earns no exemption: each identity faces the same stake.
